//: Type-checking for plain JavaScript. There is no TypeScript migration here and
there must not be one: nothing is renamed, nothing is compiled, and the files
Cloudflare Pages serves stay exactly the .js they are today. tsc runs with
--noEmit purely as a linter that understands scope.
WHY: buildOrderConfirmation referenced an undeclared `meta` and threw on every
order for weeks — no confirmation email was ever sent. create-payment-intent
called json() five times and never imported it, so every return path threw
including the catch block, and checkout was down. Both are one identifier that
does not exist. `node --check` parses fine in both cases, because an unbound
name is only an error when its line RUNS.
Scoped to functions/ on purpose. That is the money path, it is all modules
with real imports, and it is small enough to keep at zero errors. The
storefront and admin files are browser globals talking to each other through
window, which this would drown in noise for very little.
strict is OFF deliberately. The goal is 'this name does not exist', not a type
system. Turning on strictNullChecks here would produce thousands of findings
about optional fields and bury the one that matters.
